24 A microphone is connected to a cathode-ray oscilloscope (CRO). A sound wave of constant
frequency is detected by the microphone. The screen of the CRO is shown.
1.0 cm
1.0 cm
The time-base is set at 1.0 ms cm–1.
What is the frequency of the sound wave?
A
250 Hz
B
500 Hz
C
670 Hz
D
4000 Hz

hints: Count horizontal $1.0\text{ cm}$ squares for one complete repetition of the sine wave, from the same point on the wave to the next identical point.
Multiply that horizontal length in $\text{cm}$ by the time-base $1.0\text{ ms cm}^{-1}$ to get the period $T$ in $\text{ms}$.
Use $f = 1/T$ with $T$ converted to seconds, and check that the $1.0\text{ cm}$ vertical amplitude does not affect frequency.
walkthrough: Identify one full period on the CRO screen by following the trace from the left edge where it rises through the centre, through one peak and one trough, until it returns to the same rising-centre position.
Measure its horizontal length: it occupies $4.0$ squares, and each square is $1.0\text{ cm}$, so the period length is $4.0\text{ cm}$.
Apply the time-base: $T = 4.0\text{ cm} \times 1.0\text{ ms cm}^{-1} = 4.0\text{ ms} = 4.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}$.

A.explanation: One full cycle spans $4.0\text{ cm}$, giving $T = 4.0\text{ ms}$ and $f = 1/T = 250\text{ Hz}$.

B.explanation: This uses $T = 2.0\text{ ms}$ for only half a true cycle, confusing a peak-to-trough distance with a full period.

C.explanation: This does not follow from $f = 1/T$ with $T = 4.0\times 10^{-3}\text{ s}$ and the $1.0\text{ ms cm}^{-1}$ time-base.

D.explanation: This treats $1.0\text{ cm}$ as the period instead of measuring the $4.0\text{ cm}$ length of one complete wave.
